scope: Aggregate UK YouTube viewing among ages 4–15 as observed by Barb/Ofcom, not children globally and not a children's genre-only estimate

yearly_context.population: In-home YouTube viewing over connected devices; Barb measurement
In-home YouTube viewing on connected devices; Barb measurement
In-home YouTube viewing on connected devices; Barb measurement

device_context.denominator: In-home Wi-Fi YouTube viewing in the UK across measured devices

seasonal_questions.comparison: Same age cohort and territory, term weeks versus school-break weeks in the same year, controlling for bank holidays and duration
seasonal_questions.data_requirement: Official weekly or monthly age-filtered YouTube viewing series, school calendar and comparable device scope

seasonal_questions.comparison: Winter holiday versus nonholiday weeks, separate month effects and device availability
seasonal_questions.data_requirement: Children's age-specific dated watch-minute series, not year-end popularity rankings

seasonal_questions.comparison: Country-specific summer school break versus same-age term dates
seasonal_questions.data_requirement: Same-person or same-frame aggregate seasonal viewing with days observed and school-calendar mapping

seasonal_questions.comparison: Time-series reach of child-directed seasonal video category, not total YouTube viewing
seasonal_questions.data_requirement: Privacy-safe child-directed category classification and dated view-time counts, not isolated viral videos

seasonal_questions.comparison: After-school versus daytime windows in the same season, not yearly seasonal change
seasonal_questions.data_requirement: Clock-hour chart with actual numeric bins under disclosed device/age window

inferential_gates.reason: Annual averages do not supply school-term, summer or winter viewing by date
Age-group frames and measures must match; parent surveys and Barb meters cannot be pooled
YouTube use includes adults' videos watched by children, not only content labeled Made for Kids
Study uses regulator aggregate statistics only; no child-level watch history, identities or sensitive attributes

limitations: The 2024–2025 percentage change is year-over-year, not seasonal lift within either year.
TV-set share and total in-home minutes use compatible age and device scopes but measure different units; do not multiply them into unique viewers.
Barb in-home broadband viewing excludes some out-of-home and cellular traffic, so not the full viewing population.
Children's viewing time is not synonymous with Made for Kids content, preschool viewing or educational content.
Shorts, live and copyright-audio-matched selected channel audiences may be excluded from some provider-specific panels.
Child location, gender, interests, profiles, watch histories and credentials must not be collected for this research.
UK measures cannot be projected onto all countries without appropriate independent frames.
